videos.script: Every night at half past two, root runs a backup script on the portal. Anybody can edit it. {{bits}} That is nine permission bits set wrong, and one find command shows it. {{need}} Then a harder case. The accountants write the client files, an auditor only reads them, the portal reads them too. Nine bits cannot say that. {{acl}} An access control list can. You will add named entries, and meet the mask, which an ordinary chmod quietly rewrites. {{default}} Then defaults, for files nobody has created yet. {{order}} And the order Linux checks the list in, which surprises almost everybody. {{ntfs}} Last, the same ideas on Windows, where deny entries exist and win.
